results.question: Why do people save items to a wishlist in the first place?
results.restated: What are the main reasons people give for saving items to a wishlist on Indian online fashion platforms?
results.answer:
Answer
Interpretation: People say they save items mainly to defer the decision while they resolve specific doubts — led by the material & digital-physical gap (C2), price (C6), and fit & size uncertainty (C1) — with styling & self-image (C3), fulfilment concerns (C7), and external validation (C4/C10) also in play; some discussion points to intent fading after saving (C12), timing triggers (C13), or no intent at all (C9). The corpus holds nothing on how this differs between kinds of shopper.

Evidence
- Material & digital-physical gap (C2): 241 of 1,018 records; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]].
- Price (C6): 207 of 1,018 records; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]].
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1): 189 of 1,018 records; 4 sources; reliable agreement with human coder (kappa 0.657) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]].
- Styling & self-image (C3): 154 of 1,018 records; 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]].
- Fulfilment (C7): 140 of 1,018 records; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]].
- External validation & social proof (C4): 82 of 1,018 records; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]].
- External validation & social proof (C10): 68 of 1,018 records; 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]].
- Intent extinguished after saving (C12): 54 of 1,018 records; 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]].
- Action trigger (journey stage) (C13): 51 of 1,018 records; 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]].
- Intent never existed (C9): 21 of 1,018 records; 2 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C9]].

In users' words
- “there are sizing variations and differences in quality between the different colours.” [[rec|8a2701c85c668f294af3abb28f4581d32c085656]]
- “I used to buy for the ‘vibe’... I buy clothes for real life now” [[rec|f25944642b667c3d03053b6c4fda7dec7fb0c41c]]
- “I usually just wait since your phone has captured the data that you are looking for a specific product.” [[rec|653385bf09973ea5d85a71d673720b4158169736]]

Variation
- By source for fit & size uncertainty (C1): YouTube 144 of 573; Reddit 40 of 309; Play 3 of 114; App Store 2 of 22 [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]][[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]][[analysis_source_code|play|C1]][[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]].
- By source for intent extinguished after saving (C12): Reddit 42 of 309; YouTube 11 of 573; App Store 1 of 22 [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C12]][[analysis_source_code|youtube|C12]][[analysis_source_code|appstore|C12]].
- By source for action trigger (C13): Reddit 40 of 309; YouTube 9 of 573; Play 2 of 114 [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C13]][[analysis_source_code|youtube|C13]][[analysis_source_code|play|C13]].
- Interpretation: The corpus is too thin to report whether out-of-stock clutter (B2.1) varies by source in a stable way; counts are 4 of 573 on YouTube, 3 of 309 on Reddit, and 1 of 22 on the App Store [[analysis_source_code|youtube|B2.1]][[analysis_source_code|reddit|B2.1]][[analysis_source_code|appstore|B2.1]].
- Interpretation: The corpus holds nothing on how this differs between kinds of shopper; segments are derived rather than observed [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].

Counter-evidence
- Rival barriers are also frequently discussed at the same stage: styling & self-image (C3) 154 of 1,018; fulfilment (C7) 140 of 1,018; external validation & social proof (C4) 82 of 1,018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]].
- Several barriers co-occur above chance, suggesting users often mention multiple reasons together rather than a single motive:
  - Fit & size uncertainty with external validation & social proof: C1 with C10 appears together in 37 records [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]].
  - Action trigger with styling & self-image: C13 with C3 in 22 records [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C3]].
  - Intent extinguished after saving with styling & self-image: C12 with C3 in 22 records [[analysis_cooccurrence|C12|C3]].
  - Action trigger with price: C13 with C6 in 20 records [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]].
- Interpretation: Because of these co-occurrences, a single “main reason” for saving is not isolated by this corpus.

Confidence
- Medium. Fit & size uncertainty (C1) shows reliable agreement with the human coder (kappa 0.657) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]], but several relevant codes lack measurable reliability and two validation thresholds fail at the corpus level [[analysis_gold_agreement|C13]][[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]]. Source triangulation spans roughly three independent types, not four [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].

Limitations
- This corpus measures discussion, not behavior; shares are of what people chose to post, not save or purchase rates [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow and likely under-represents price/value and delivery/trust topics; rankings are conditional on that filter [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- The corpus holds nothing on how motives differ between kinds of shopper; segments are derived rather than observed and cannot support segment-level claims [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].
- Silent forgetting is under-detected by construction, so absence of Stage A signals cannot be read as infrequent [[analysis_method_flags|stage_a_underdetection]].
- Only about 36% of relevant discussion is Myntra-specific; platform-mechanical interpretations rest on a smaller pool [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Small counts are reportable but not rankable; treat codes near the floor cautiously [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].
gate_reasons: the corpus holds nothing on how this differs between kinds of shopper
gate_caveats: how often this is raised: too thin to report for B2.1
whether this holds up across sources: too thin to report for B2.1

results.question: What stops people from buying the things they have saved?
results.restated: Which barriers, as raised in the analysed public discussion, explain why people do not buy items they saved to wishlists on Indian online fashion platforms?
results.answer:
Answer
People most often pause at item-level doubts after saving: the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2), price (C6), and fit & size uncertainty (C1). Fulfilment worries (C7) also appear frequently; styling/self-image (C3) and reviews/social proof (C4) are present but raised less often. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]]

Evidence
- Material & digital-physical gap (C2): 241 of 1,018 records; 226 distinct authors; raised across 4 sources; Stage C. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]]
- Price (C6): 207 of 1,018; 189 distinct authors; across 4 sources; Stage C; coded as an eliminator with exit. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]]
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1): 189 of 1,018; 185 distinct authors; across 4 sources; Stage C. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]]
- Fulfilment (C7): 140 of 1,018; 137 distinct authors; across 4 sources; Stage C; coded as an eliminator with exit. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]]
- Styling & self-image (C3): 154 of 1,018; 142 distinct authors; across 3 sources; Stage C. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]]
- External validation & social proof — reviews from recipients (C4): 82 of 1,018; 80 distinct authors; across 4 sources; Stage C. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]]
- Partner/peer check (C10): 68 of 1,018; 67 distinct authors; across 3 sources; Stage C. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]]
- Intent extinguished after saving (C12): 54 of 1,018; 49 distinct authors; across 3 sources; Stage C; coded as exit. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]]
- Action trigger (C13): 51 of 1,018; 50 distinct authors; across 3 sources; Stage C. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]]
- Comparison & decision load (C5): 22 of 1,018; 22 distinct authors; across 3 sources; Stage C; below the threshold to rank. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C5]] [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]]

Journey stage
- The leading barriers are concentrated at Stage C (item-level decision): C2, C6, C1, C7, C3, C4, C10, C12, and C13 are all recorded at Stage C. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]]
- Stage A is present but smaller in the captured discussion: Wishlist entry point buried (A2.1) appears in 47 of 1,018 records. [[analysis_code_prevalence|A2.1]]

Source mix
- C2 appears on YouTube (116/573), Reddit (104/309), Play (18/114), and App Store (3/22). [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C2]]
- C6 appears on Reddit (74/309), YouTube (70/573), Play (60/114), and App Store (3/22). [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C6]]
- C1 appears on YouTube (144/573), Reddit (40/309), Play (3/114), and App Store (2/22). [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]]
- C7 appears on YouTube (67/573), Reddit (46/309), Play (22/114), and App Store (5/22). [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C7]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C7]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C7]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C7]]
- C4 appears on YouTube (43/573), Reddit (33/309), Play (3/114), and App Store (3/22). [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C4]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C4]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C4]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C4]]
- C5 is present but thin across Reddit (12/309), YouTube (9/573), and App Store (1/22). [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C5]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C5]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C5]]

Compound problems (co-occurrence)
- C2 often appears with reviews/social proof (C4): 53 joint records; lift=2.73. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]]
- C2 often appears with fulfilment (C7): 65 joint records; lift=1.961. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]]
- Fit & size (C1) co-occurs with styling/self-image (C3): 40 joint records; lift=1.399. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C3]]
- Fit & size (C1) co-occurs with partner/peer check (C10): 37 joint records; lift=2.931. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]]
- Action trigger (C13) co-occurs with price (C6): 20 joint records; lift=1.929. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]]

Addressable opportunities vs. low or no intent
- Barriers where removing friction could plausibly convert saved items: C2 (241/1,018, defer), C1 (189/1,018, defer), C3 (154/1,018, defer), C4 (82/1,018, defer), C10 (68/1,018, defer), and C13 (51/1,018, trigger, defer). [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]]
- Barriers signaling hard exits even after saving: Price (C6; 207/1,018, eliminator, exit), Fulfilment (C7; 140/1,018, eliminator, exit), and Intent extinguished (C12; 54/1,018, exit). [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]]
- Interpretation: Comparison & decision load (C5; 22/1,018) is mentioned but too thin to prioritise confidently in ordering. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C5]] [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]]

In users' words
- “3 star is for most of the images not being the same as shown in pictures.” [[rec|45a8341fa1843b03574e839eed8ea6a7c902f9b8]]
- “Accessories have problems as the size shown in 3 products that I bought was wrong” [[rec|45a8341fa1843b03574e839eed8ea6a7c902f9b8]]
- “myntra is 2x the price of meesho” [[rec|ba4d67eb593d2a741cfb697a26e52fad442ce46d]]
- “I would prefer local shops and street shopping, so so much better” [[rec|0afe1663f365d89029adf08a61c57bd3b6f623c7]]

Variation
- By source: C2 is raised on all four sources, with Reddit (104/309) and YouTube (116/573) both contributing substantial shares; Play and App Store are smaller but present. [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C2]]
- By barrier reliability: Fit & size (C1) and Price (C6) are supported by reliable coder agreement; C2 is weaker on agreement; C4, C5, and C7 have unknown reliability due to too few gold labels. [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C5]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C7]]
- By journey stage: The discussion concentrates at Stage C; Stage A factors exist but are less visible in posts. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|A2.1]] [[analysis_method_flags|stage_a_underdetection]]
- Interpretation: Cross-source triangulation reflects roughly three independent source types, as Play and App Store share review-skew characteristics. [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]]

Counter-evidence
- Rival explanations within the same stage include Styling & self-image (C3; 154/1,018), Partner/peer check (C10; 68/1,018), Intent extinguished (C12; 54/1,018), Action trigger (C13; 51/1,018), and Wishlist entry point buried (A2.1; 47/1,018). [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|A2.1]]
- Several barriers tend not to appear alone: C2 with C4 (53 joint; lift=2.73) and C2 with C7 (65 joint; lift=1.961) suggest that doubts about real-world look co-occur with the need for trusted reviews and with fulfilment concerns. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]]

Confidence
Medium. Large sample sizes for the leading barriers and presence across four sources support stability (e.g., C2 241/1,018; C6 207/1,018; C1 189/1,018) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]], and coder agreement is reliable for C1 and C6 [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]]. However, agreement for C2 is weaker [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]], several other codes are not measurable [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C5]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C7]], and two validation thresholds fail at the corpus level. [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]]

Limitations
- These shares measure discussion, not behaviour; no funnel or conversion data is present. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]]
- The relevance rubric is narrow; recall is estimated lower and likely under-captures price/value and delivery/trust topics, so rankings are conditional. [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]]
- Stage A factors are under-detected by construction; low counts there are not evidence of low incidence. [[analysis_method_flags|stage_a_underdetection]]
- Only about 36% of records are Myntra-specific; platform-mechanical reads should be taken cautiously for Myntra in particular. [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]]
- App-store sources share review skew; effective triangulation reflects roughly three independent source types, not four. [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]]
- Two validation thresholds fail; per-code reliability varies, with some codes weak or not measurable. [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C5]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C7]]
- Price (C6) is a major barrier but direct monetary incentives are out of scope; interpret as an information/timing problem rather than a call for discounts. [[analysis_method_flags|no_monetary_incentive]]
- Counts below 30 (e.g., C5) are reportable but not rankable. [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]]
- Segments based on decision state are derived from codes, not observed; associations with “undecided” are partly circular. [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]]
gate_caveats: an ordering of these barriers: too thin to report for C5
whether this holds up across sources: too thin to report for C5

results.question: What are people still uncertain about at the moment they decide whether to buy?
results.restated: Which specific uncertainties do people still have at the moment they must decide whether to buy an item (the item-decision stage)?
results.answer:
Answer
At the item-decision stage, the biggest uncertainties people raise are the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2), price and timing (C6), which size to pick (C1), and whether it suits their self-image or wardrobe (C3), with material/appearance worries discussed slightly more often than price, and price slightly more often than fit and styling [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]]. These often come as compound problems, especially material doubts paired with wanting to read real-customer reviews and with return anxiety [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]][[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]].

Evidence
- The gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2): 241 of 1,018 discussion instances; share of discussion 0.237; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]].
- Price (C6): 207 of 1,018; share 0.203; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]].
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1): 189 of 1,018; share 0.186; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]].
- Styling & self-image (C3): 154 of 1,018; share 0.151; 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]].
- Fulfilment (returns/exchange burden) (C7): 140 of 1,018; share 0.138; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]].
- External validation from reviews (C4): 82 of 1,018; share 0.081; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]].
- External validation & social proof — check with partner (C10): 68 of 1,018; share 0.067; 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]].
- Intent extinguished after saving (C12): 54 of 1,018; share 0.053; 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]].
- Action trigger (C13): 51 of 1,018; share 0.05; 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]].
- External validation & social proof — go elsewhere to check (C14): 38 of 1,018; share 0.037; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C14]].
- Comparison & decision load (C5) is present but thin: 22 of 1,018; share 0.022; 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C5]].

Co-occurrence (compound problems)
- C2 with external validation from reviews (C4): 53 joint mentions; above-chance pairing [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]].
- C2 with fulfilment (C7): 65 joint mentions; above-chance pairing [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]].
- Styling (C3) with action trigger (C13): 22 joint mentions; above-chance pairing [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C3]].
- Styling (C3) with intent extinguished after saving (C12): 22 joint mentions; above-chance pairing [[analysis_cooccurrence|C12|C3]].
- Fit (C1) with “check with partner” social proof (C10): 37 joint mentions; above-chance pairing [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]].

Fine-grained sub-themes (what exactly within C1, C2, C3)
- Fit & size (C1) subcodes within 189 C1 mentions:
  - C1.1: 82; share within C1 0.434 [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.1]].
  - C1.2: 49; share 0.259 [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.2]].
  - C1.3: 25; share 0.132 [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.3]].
  - C1.4: 19; share 0.101 [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.4]].
  - unclear: 24; share 0.127 [[analysis_subcode|C1|unclear]].
- Material & digital-physical gap (C2) subcodes within 241 C2 mentions:
  - C2.4: 146; share within C2 0.606 [[analysis_subcode|C2|C2.4]].
  - C2.1: 87; share 0.361 [[analysis_subcode|C2|C2.1]].
  - C2.2: 37; share 0.154 [[analysis_subcode|C2|C2.2]].
  - C2.3: 27; share 0.112 [[analysis_subcode|C2|C2.3]].
  - C2.5: 16; share 0.066 [[analysis_subcode|C2|C2.5]].
  - unclear: 38; share 0.158 [[analysis_subcode|C2|unclear]].
- Styling & self-image (C3) subcodes within 154 C3 mentions:
  - C3.1: 119; share within C3 0.773 [[analysis_subcode|C3|C3.1]].
  - C3.2: 44; share 0.286 [[analysis_subcode|C3|C3.2]].
  - C3.3: 41; share 0.266 [[analysis_subcode|C3|C3.3]].
  - C3.4: 24; share 0.156 [[analysis_subcode|C3|C3.4]].
  - C3.5: 29; share 0.188 [[analysis_subcode|C3|C3.5]].
  - unclear: 34; share 0.221 [[analysis_subcode|C3|unclear]].
Interpretation: The subcodes are enumerated but not labeled in the brief, so we can report their relative presence but not name their specific meanings.

Workarounds and intent signals
- People explicitly consult reviews as a workaround before buying: “solution read product reviews then buy.” [[rec|45a8341fa1843b03574e839eed8ea6a7c902f9b8]].
- People defer purchases to wait for better options/prices to surface across sites: “I usually just wait since your phone has captured the data that you are looking for a specific product. It’ll eventually show up in multiple sites.” [[rec|653385bf09973ea5d85a71d673720b4158169736]].
Interpretation: These show intent often survives the uncertainty, with actions taken to reduce it rather than abandoning immediately.

In users' words
- “most of the images not being the same as shown in pictures” [[rec|45a8341fa1843b03574e839eed8ea6a7c902f9b8]].
- “solution read product reviews then buy.” [[rec|45a8341fa1843b03574e839eed8ea6a7c902f9b8]].
- “And I'm 5'7, should I buy an overcoat?” [[rec|a91133402e1ca1100b362aaf8833b2d3cb8d6c61]].
- “people have a limited amount of pants, unlike tops” [[rec|349ae8b0c2942f92601d97c5d24cd2f7228a6d1d]].

Variation
- Presence across sources:
  - C2 appears on YouTube (116 of 573; share 0.202), Reddit (104 of 309; share 0.337), Play (18 of 114; share 0.158), and App Store (3 of 22; share 0.136) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C2]][[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]][[analysis_source_code|play|C2]][[analysis_source_code|appstore|C2]].
  - C6 appears on Reddit (74 of 309; share 0.239) and YouTube (70 of 573; share 0.122) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]][[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]].
  - C1 appears on YouTube (144 of 573; share 0.251), Reddit (40 of 309; share 0.129), Play (3 of 114; share 0.026), and App Store (2 of 22; share 0.091) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]][[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]][[analysis_source_code|play|C1]][[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]].
  - C3 appears on Reddit (99 of 309; share 0.32), YouTube (53 of 573; share 0.092), and Play (2 of 114; share 0.018) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C3]][[analysis_source_code|youtube|C3]][[analysis_source_code|play|C3]].
Interpretation: The leading uncertainties show up across multiple source types, which supports generality, but the app-store slices are smaller and review-skewed.

Counter-evidence
- Rival barriers at the same stage also draw discussion: fulfilment (C7) at 140 of 1,018 (share 0.138), external validation with partner (C10) at 68 of 1,018 (share 0.067), intent extinguished after saving (C12) at 54 of 1,018 (share 0.053), action trigger (C13) at 51 of 1,018 (share 0.05), and “go check elsewhere” validation (C14) at 38 of 1,018 (share 0.037) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C14]].
- Several barriers rarely appear alone, with above-chance co-occurrence indicating compounded doubts rather than a single-cause blocker: C2 with C4 (53 joint mentions), C2 with C7 (65), C1 with C10 (37), C3 with C13 (22), and C3 with C12 (22) [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]][[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]][[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]][[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C3]][[analysis_cooccurrence|C12|C3]].

Confidence
Medium. The leading codes have substantial counts and appear across three to four source types (e.g., C2 at 241 of 1,018 with 4 sources; C6 at 207 of 1,018 with 4 sources) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]]. Reliability against human coding is strong for Fit (C1; kappa 0.657) and Price (C6; kappa 0.645) but weaker for Material (C2; kappa 0.427) and Styling (C3; kappa 0.515), so orderings that rely on C2/C3 are provisional [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C3]]. Two validation thresholds fail overall, and relevance recall is estimated at about 79% against an 85% target [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].

Limitations
- This is discussion share, not behavioral conversion: the corpus measures what people chose to talk about, not what shoppers did or how many dropped off [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow; hand-read recall was near 45% and exclusions skew toward price/value and delivery/trust, so the ranking reflects a constrained slice of item-decision talk [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Platform specificity: only about 36% is Myntra-specific; most evidence generalizes to Indian online fashion rather than Myntra alone [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Source independence: app stores are not independent of each other, and Reddit was collected via a third party; treat “three source types,” not four, as the basis for triangulation [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Segment caveat: segments derive from the codes themselves; lifts into “undecided” are partly circular [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].

results.question: What makes people postpone a purchase rather than abandon it altogether?
results.restated: What factors discussed in the corpus make people postpone a saved-item purchase (defer it) rather than abandoning it permanently?
results.answer:
Answer
People most often postpone because of the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) and fit & size uncertainty (C1); purchase is more likely to be abandoned when price (C6) or fulfilment/returns friction (C7) dominate. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]]

Evidence
- How the corpus marks outcomes: at the main decision stage, posts coded as defer number 526 of 1018, while exit is 199 of 1018. Across the whole corpus, earlier and later stages are much smaller. [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|exit]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|A|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|B|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|D|exit]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|Z|defer]]
- Barriers associated with Defer at the main decision stage:
  - Material & digital-physical gap (C2): 241 of 1018. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]]
  - Fit & size uncertainty (C1): 189 of 1018. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]]
  - Styling & self-image (C3): 154 of 1018. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]]
  - External validation & social proof — what recipients said (C4): 82 of 1018. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]]
  - External validation & social proof — check with partner (C10): 68 of 1018. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]]
  - Action trigger (journey stage) (C13): 51 of 1018. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]]

- Barriers associated with Exit:
  - Price (C6): 207 of 1018. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]]
  - Fulfilment (C7): 140 of 1018. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]]
  - Intent extinguished — “Do I still actually want this?” (C12): 54 of 1018. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]]
  - Intent extinguished — “I already bought something like it somewhere else.” (C11): 24 of 1018. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C11]]
- Counterfactual “I would have bought if X changed,” for Defer-related barriers:
  - Action trigger (C13): 12 of 49 records express explicit counterfactual purchase intent. [[analysis_counterfactuals|C13]]

- Co-occurring barriers that accompany Defer (compound causes):
  - Fit & size uncertainty (C1) with “check with partner” (C10): 37 joint records, above chance. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]]

In users' words

- “so it's better if u try it at their offline store and then proceed to purchase” [[rec|dff1e8c42ec7425a8260683d42a33b842ef9265c]]

Variation
- By source: Fit & size uncertainty (C1) appears more often on YouTube (144 of 573) than on Reddit (40 of 309), with smaller counts on Play (3 of 114) and App Store (2 of 22). [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]]
- By source: Action trigger (C13) appears on Reddit (40 of 309) and YouTube (9 of 573), with very small counts on Play (2 of 114). [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C13]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C13]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C13]]
- Interpretation: The brief does not provide a segment breakdown by urgency/decision state beyond the code-phase attribution, and segments are derived rather than observed.

Counter-evidence
- Price (C6) and Fulfilment (C7) are strongly associated with Exit rather than Defer, with 207 of 1018 and 140 of 1018 respectively. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]]
- Intent extinguished after saving (C12 and C11) also aligns with Exit, at 54 of 1018 and 24 of 1018. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C11]]
- Co-occurrence shows compound causes: for example, the “already bought elsewhere” variant (C11) frequently appears with Price (C6) in 15 joint records, above chance. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C11|C6]]

Confidence
Medium. Core defer and exit signals rely on sizeable counts at the main decision stage (e.g., 526 defer, 199 exit of 1018), and several key codes (C1, C6) show reliable agreement with the human coder. [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|exit]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]] However, multiple codes central to this question (C13, C7, C11) lack measurable reliability, and two validation thresholds fail. [[analysis_gold_agreement|C13]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C7]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C11]] [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]]

Limitations
- This is discussion share, not behavior; no funnel or conversion data exist. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]]
- The relevance rubric is narrow and likely under-represents price/value and delivery/trust topics; rankings are conditional on that filter. [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]]
- Only about 36% of relevant posts are Myntra-specific; platform claims rest on a smaller pool. [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]]
- Several codes used here lack measurable reliability, and two evaluation thresholds fail; interpret magnitudes with caution. [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]]
- Segments are derived from the coding scheme rather than observed user states; lifts into “undecided” are partly circular. [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]]
- Source diversity is effectively three independent types; app-store reviews share a skew. [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]]
- Some cited phenomena have small counts in certain sources; findings below common floors should not be ranked. [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]]

Interpretation: Definitions
- “Postpone/Defer” refers to records where the user’s barrier sits in confidence/trigger phases without an extinguished intent, coded with outcome=defer at the main decision stage; “abandon/Exit” refers to records coded with outcome=exit, including eliminators and extinguished-intent cases. This interpretation aligns with the stage-outcome tallies but is not an observed behavioral outcome. [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|exit]]

results.question: What do people go looking for outside the app before they buy?
results.restated: What do shoppers go looking for off the app (outside the platform) before they buy an item they saved to a wishlist?
results.answer:
Answer
People most often say they go off‑app to resolve the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2), to check price (C6), and to sort out fit & size uncertainty (C1); social proof checks (C4/C14) also appear, but less often than those three [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C14]].

Evidence
- Material & digital-physical gap (C2): 241 of 1018 records; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]].
- Price (C6): 207 of 1018 records; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]].
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1): 189 of 1018 records; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]].
- Styling & self-image (C3): 154 of 1018 records; 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]].
- External validation & social proof via reviews/UGC (C4): 82 of 1018 records; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]].
- External validation & social proof via off‑app checks (C14): 38 of 1018 records; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C14]].

In users' words
- “Bro in Ajio app there is no customer rating & reviews option?then how can we know that products are quality or not? without reviews?” [[rec|aea48d3f4b52061090c5e983ad2790dd364cab14]]
- “ये app तो भाव (price) में बहुत ही खतरनाक है भया ।” [[rec|58a94f0fdde31e279de85e268e24bb4e462ec6d3]]
- “Accessories have problems as the size shown in 3 products that I bought was wrong … 3 star is for most of the images not being the same as shown in pictures. solution read product reviews then buy.” [[rec|45a8341fa1843b03574e839eed8ea6a7c902f9b8]]
- “i go for zara because i can get full length jeans there” [[rec|cb9e25e38bc4cdd0ea4a11e289f06d91dadaec33]]

Variation
- By source, material & digital-physical gap (C2) is raised most on Reddit (104 of 309) and also present on YouTube (116 of 573), Play (18 of 114), and App Store (3 of 22) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C2]].
- Price (C6) is especially prominent in Play Store reviews (60 of 114), and also present on Reddit (74 of 309), YouTube (70 of 573), and App Store (3 of 22) [[analysis_source_code|play|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C6]].
- Fit & size (C1) is discussed more on YouTube (144 of 573) than Reddit (40 of 309), with smaller counts on Play (3 of 114) and App Store (2 of 22) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]].
- External validation & social proof via off‑app checks (C14) appears across Reddit (19 of 309), YouTube (17 of 573), App Store (1 of 22), and Play (1 of 114) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C14]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C14]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C14]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C14]].
- Interpretation: Off‑app checks are not concentrated in a single platform; the major off‑app motivations (C2, C6, C1) appear across multiple source types as shown by their presence on 3–4 sources each [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C14]].

Compound behaviors (co‑occurrence)
- Material & digital-physical gap (C2) with external validation & social proof via reviews/UGC (C4): 53 joint mentions, indicating people pair fabric/colour doubt with seeking outside reviews [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]].
- Material & digital-physical gap (C2) with fulfilment (C7): 65 joint mentions, tying fabric/colour doubt to return/handling considerations [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]].
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1) with external validation & social proof (C10): 37 joint mentions, suggesting size checks alongside checking with others [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]].
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1) with styling & self-image (C3): 40 joint mentions; material gap (C2) with styling & self-image (C3): 47 joint mentions, indicating product‑info checks cluster together [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C3]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C3]].
- Price (C6) with action trigger (C13): 20 joint mentions, linking price checks to timing decisions [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]].

Counter-evidence
- Other rival concerns also drive discussion in this stage: fulfilment (C7) appears in 140 of 1018 records, and external validation & social proof (C10) in 68 of 1018; intent extinguished after saving (C12) in 54 of 1018; action trigger (C13) in 51 of 1018; availability at decision time (C8) in 35 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C8]].
- Interpretation: These do not negate off‑app checks but show that off‑app motivations sit alongside worries about returns, whether to proceed now, and whether sizes are in stock.

Confidence
Medium. The leading signals (C1, C6) have reliable agreement with a human coder (kappa 0.66 and 0.64), while material & digital-physical gap (C2) and styling & self-image (C3) are weaker (kappa 0.43 and 0.52), and external‑validation codes (C4, C14) are not measurable for reliability [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C3]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C14]]. Method flags also note two validation thresholds failing and an estimated relevance recall below target [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].

Limitations
- The shares reported are of discussion, not behavior; this corpus does not measure user‑level funnels or conversion rates [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- The relevance rubric is narrower than a broad save‑to‑purchase frame and likely under‑captures price/value and delivery/trust topics; rankings are conditional on that rubric [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Only about 36% of the relevant corpus is Myntra‑specific; most evidence reflects Indian online fashion shopping generally [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Source independence is limited: Play and App Store are one type; Reddit access is via a third‑party; triangulation spans roughly three independent types [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Several codes have weak or unmeasured reliability (C2, C3, C4, C14), so fine‑grained ordering across these should be treated as provisional [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C3]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C14]].
- Counts below 30 are reportable but not rankable; use caution with lower‑n signals like C14 [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].
- Price is a major barrier but the project forbids monetary incentives; interpret C6 as pointing to transparency/timing rather than discounting [[analysis_method_flags|no_monetary_incentive]].

results.question: Are people who wishlist actually intending to buy, or just bookmarking?
results.restated: Do people who add items to wishlists actually intend to buy them, or are they mostly just bookmarking for reference?
results.answer:
Answer
Partial: The corpus cannot tell us how this differs between kinds of shopper; it only shows what people who chose to post said. In that discussion, some wishlisting is clearly bookmarking with no purchase intent, and much of the rest reflects live intent that stalls on specific doubts like fit, reviews, and triggers to act [[analysis_addressable|c9_no_live_intent]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]].

Evidence
- How much is “just bookmarking” vs intent:
  - Intent never existed — the gap between saving and intending to buy (C9): 21 of 1018 records (share 0.021) [[analysis_addressable|c9_no_live_intent]].
  - Collectors — saving as a taste archive (segment, not a barrier): 126 of 1018 records (share 0.124) [[analysis_addressable|collectors]].
- Signals of live intent and the doubts that stall it:
  - Fit & size uncertainty (C1): 189 of 1018 (share 0.186) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]].
  - External validation & social proof — reviews from receivers (C4): 82 of 1018 (share 0.081) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]].
  - Action trigger (journey stage) (C13): 51 of 1018 (share 0.05) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]].
  - Intent extinguished after saving — “Do I still actually want this?” (C12): 54 of 1018 (share 0.053) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]].
  - Intent extinguished after saving — “I already bought something like it somewhere else.” (C11): 24 of 1018 (share 0.024) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C11]].
- Explicit counterfactuals — “I would have bought if …”:
  - Action trigger (C13): 12 of 49 records with C13 include a counterfactual (share 0.245) [[analysis_counterfactuals|C13]].
  - External validation & social proof (C4): 15 of 77 (share 0.195) [[analysis_counterfactuals|C4]].
  - Intent doubts after saving (C12): 8 of 52 (share 0.154) [[analysis_counterfactuals|C12]].
  - Bought elsewhere (C11): 3 of 23 (share 0.13) [[analysis_counterfactuals|C11]].
  - Fit & size (C1): 5 of 177 (share 0.028) [[analysis_counterfactuals|C1]].
  - No counterfactuals appear where intent never existed (C9): 0 of 20 (share 0) [[analysis_counterfactuals|C9]].
- Workarounds — effort despite barriers (surviving intent):
  - External validation & social proof (C4): 17 of 77 include a workaround (share 0.221; mean_effort 1.941; intensity_index 0.429) [[analysis_workaround|C4]].
  - Fit & size (C1): 17 of 177 (share 0.096; mean_effort 1.412; intensity_index 0.136) [[analysis_workaround|C1]].
  - None for “intent never existed” (C9): 0 of 20 [[analysis_workaround|C9]].
- Source mix (whether one source dominates): Fit & size (C1) appears across YouTube 144/573, Reddit 40/309, Play 3/114, App Store 2/22; External validation (C4) across YouTube 43/573, Reddit 33/309, Play 3/114, App Store 3/22; Action trigger (C13) across Reddit 40/309, YouTube 9/573, Play 2/114 [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C4]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C4]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C4]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C4]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C13]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C13]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C13]].

In users' words
- “I was cleaning my wishlist yesterday and realised half the clothes I save are not for anything I actually have planned” [[rec|6102d72a4134c75fd1e23e0da192954f39145fbd]].
- “see how many posts, comments and reviews did it get” [[rec|0afe1663f365d89029adf08a61c57bd3b6f623c7]].

Variation
- By segment: Interpretation: The corpus does not separate urgent/decided buyers from casual savers in a way that lets us compare them; this gap is unfilled by the data.
- By source: Fit & size (C1) and External validation (C4) appear across Reddit, YouTube, and app-store reviews; Action trigger (C13) is strongest on Reddit and present on YouTube and Play [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C4]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C13]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C13]].
- For bought-elsewhere (C11): Interpretation: counts are small across sources, so cross-source consistency is too thin to report beyond presence [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C11]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C11]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C11]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C11]].

Counter-evidence
- Other, often larger, barriers at the same stage appear more frequently in discussion: the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) 241/1018; Price (C6) 207/1018; Styling & self-image (C3) 154/1018; Fulfilment (C7) 140/1018; External validation & social proof — check with partner (C10) 68/1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]].
- Co-occurrence suggests these doubts cluster rather than act alone: bought-elsewhere (C11) with Price (C6) n_joint=15; Fit (C1) with check-with-partner (C10) n_joint=37; Action trigger (C13) with Styling (C3) n_joint=22; Digital-physical gap (C2) with reviews-from-receivers (C4) n_joint=53; Intent-doubt-after-saving (C12) with Styling (C3) n_joint=22; Action trigger (C13) with Price (C6) n_joint=20 [[analysis_cooccurrence|C11|C6]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C3]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C12|C3]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]].

Confidence
Medium. The corpus is sizeable (1018 records), and Fit & size (C1) shows reliable agreement with the human coder (kappa 0.657) [[analysis_addressable|corpus]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]]. However, most other key codes here are not measurable for reliability, and two validation thresholds fail at the metric level [[analysis_gold_agreement|C11]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C13]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]] [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].

Limitations
- These are shares of discussion, not conversion or drop-off rates; no funnel or user-level data exists here [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow and likely under-represents price/value and delivery/trust topics; rankings are conditional on what was admitted [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Only about 36% of the relevant material is Myntra-specific; most comments concern Indian online fashion generally [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Segments are derived, not observed; we cannot cleanly compare urgent/decided buyers vs casual savers from this corpus [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].
- The source mix reflects roughly three independent source types, with known app-store skew and third-party Reddit collection [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Counts below the reporting floors should not be ranked; some codes here (e.g., bought-elsewhere C11) are near those thresholds [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].

Interpretation: Taken together, a small but real slice of wishlist talk is pure bookmarking (C9 and Collectors), while much more of the conversation shows live intent that pauses on fit, proof from other buyers, and the trigger to act; some of that intent survives via workarounds, and some extinguishes over time (C12/C11) [[analysis_addressable|c9_no_live_intent]] [[analysis_addressable|collectors]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]] [[analysis_workaround|C4]] [[analysis_workaround|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C11]].

results.question: Do different kinds of shoppers get stuck in different ways?
results.restated: Do different shopper segments (the re-cut segments of the item-decision stage: e.g. decided vs undecided, urgent vs non-urgent) get stuck on different barriers when they save items to wishlists?
results.answer:
Answer
Yes. Different shopper segments talk about different barriers after saving items, with clear skews by segment: price (C6) dominates for Committed Waiters and Hesitant Waiters, fit & size uncertainty (C1) and the material & digital-physical gap (C2) stand out for Stuck Deciders, and intent extinguished after saving (C12) is the defining theme for Lapsed Intenders. Evidence

Limitations
- This is discussion share, not behavior. No funnel or conversion data; do not read shares as what users did. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]]

results.question: Do users trust influencer reviews?
results.restated: How often and in what ways do people in this corpus express trust or distrust in influencer reviews when deciding whether to buy items they saved to wishlists on Indian online fashion platforms?
results.answer:
Answer
Interpretation: The corpus does not separate influencer content from ordinary buyer reviews, so we cannot count influencer-trust discussion directly; what we do see is limited, anecdotal mentions alongside broader talk about external validation via real-buyer evidence and off‑platform checks. External validation from real buyers (C4) appears in 82 of 1018 records and 80 distinct authors, while off‑platform verification exits (C14) appear in 38 of 1018 records and 36 distinct authors, suggesting people discuss proof and checks more often than influencer trust per se [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C14]].

Evidence
- External validation & social proof — real-buyer evidence (C4): 82 of 1018 records; 80 distinct authors; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]].
- External validation & social proof — off-platform verification exit (C14): 38 of 1018 records; 36 distinct authors; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C14]].
- Styling & self-image (C3), where a user explicitly references an influencer’s effect on desire: 154 of 1018 records; 142 distinct authors; 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]].
- Co-occurrence: material & digital-physical gap (C2) with real-buyer evidence (C4) appears together in 53 joint records, indicating checks for “what people who actually received it say” often accompany concerns about photos vs reality [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]].

In users' words
- “I liked the influencer wearing that thing more than I liked that thing by itself.” [[rec|3b77838016c90a379f151c83c5b5215067c90912]]
- “You can trust saree shops online and on instagram. I would say first see how many posts, comments and reviews did it get” [[rec|0afe1663f365d89029adf08a61c57bd3b6f623c7]]
- “Get the first in your size it will look so pretty on u trust me honest advice ❤” [[rec|f1502a27c3c1379de8dee6bb7c9b858195fa4e3f]]

Variation
Interpretation: Because influencer content is not separated from buyer reviews, we cannot measure source- or segment-level variation for influencer trust specifically. As a proxy for off‑platform checking (C14), discussion appears on Reddit (19 of 309) and YouTube (17 of 573), with isolated mentions in app stores (1 of 22; 1 of 114) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C14]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C14]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C14]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C14]]. Interpretation: The brief flags that whether this holds up across sources is too thin to report for C5, and overall support is too thin to rank for several adjacent codes.

Counter-evidence
- Rival barriers are discussed more often than any influencer-anchored trust theme: fit & size uncertainty (C1) at 189 of 1018, fulfilment (C7) at 140 of 1018, price (C6) at 207 of 1018, and styling & self-image (C3) at 154 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]].
- Off‑platform verification does not necessarily imply influencer trust; one user emphasizes posts/comments/reviews and then prefers “local shops and street shopping,” which points away from relying on influencers [[rec|0afe1663f365d89029adf08a61c57bd3b6f623c7]].

Confidence
Low. Influencer trust is not directly coded; C2 and C3 have weak coder agreement, C4 and C14 are not measurable for reliability, and two validation thresholds fail at the metric level [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C3]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C14]] [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].

Limitations
- The corpus does not separate influencer content from ordinary buyer reviews; any influencer signal is inferred from verbatim mentions and adjacent validation codes. Interpretation: This constrains all counts to proxies rather than influencer‑specific measures.
- Every share reported is a share of discussion, not behaviour; there is no funnel or conversion data here [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow and likely under-represents price/value and delivery/trust talk; rankings are conditional on what was included [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Source independence is limited to roughly three source types; Reddit access is via a third party and app-store reviews have known skews [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Only about 36% of the material is Myntra‑specific; much of this concerns Indian online fashion generally [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Some counts are near or below reporting floors (e.g., C14=38); thin slices should not be ranked [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].
- Segments are derived, not observed; any segment lift for confidence-phase doubts is partly circular [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].

Evidence
- Material & digital-physical gap (C2): 241 of 1,018 posts; 4 sources; mean confidence 0.773 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]].

Variation
- By source (examples shown where available):
  - Fit & size uncertainty (C1): YouTube 144 of 573; Reddit 40 of 309; Play 3 of 114; App Store 2 of 22 [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]].

  - C13 with C3: 22 joint records [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C3]].
  - C12 with C3: 22 joint records [[analysis_cooccurrence|C12|C3]].

- Medium. C1 and C6 are marked reliable by agreement with a human coder (kappa 0.66 and 0.64 respectively) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]]. C4 and D1 are not measurable for reliability [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|D1]]. Method-wide thresholds failed for two validation gates, and overall recall is estimated at about 79%, not measured at the 85% target [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].

- No demographic split: Interpretation: The corpus contains no reliable author-level gender labels or demographics, so it cannot support any claim about gender differences.
- Instrument is discussion, not behavior: every share is a share of discussion, not a conversion or drop-off rate; no user- or funnel-level data exists [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- Coding reliability: two validation thresholds failed; only some codes clear reliability; C10 is explicitly unreliable (kappa 0.10) and any claim resting on it must carry this caveat [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]] [[analysis_method_flags|c10_unreliable]].

- Any consistent proxy to infer gender, and how often? Interpretation: Occasional self-references appear but are inconsistent and not reliable as a proxy. Interpretation: Such language is not a consistent or validated gender label across the corpus.

Interpretation: We would need explicit, reliable gender labels per author and sufficient per-gender counts for each barrier across multiple independent source types; the current corpus does not provide this.

- What evidence within the corpus would contradict a claim that men and women experience different dominant barriers? Interpretation: None specific to gender; however, the overall prominence of Material & digital-physical gap (C2), Price (C6), and Fit & size uncertainty (C1) suggests widely shared discussion topics rather than clearly gendered patterns [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]].

- “It’s about the fit and silhouette.” … “Indian brands have managed to copy the look of Zara, but not the fit” [[rec|7da7de1a996e937c2dc91a995f8f2402f23e8818]].
- “same sizing issue” … “one jean that would have fit u properly at a particular size, at the same size another jeans may not fit u” [[rec|dff1e8c42ec7425a8260683d42a33b842ef9265c]].

Variation
- By source in this window, C1 is discussed more often on YouTube (144/573) than on Reddit (40/309), with smaller counts on Google Play (3/114) and the App Store (2/22) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]], [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]].
- Interpretation: The brief does not provide dates for records, so we cannot show counts per month or year for C1, assess whether coverage is sufficient in each period, or test for real change over time.
- Interpretation: The brief does not report posting rates or changing source composition over time; we cannot assess whether shifts in source mix could mimic a trend.
- Interpretation: There is no evidence here about classifier or codebook changes over the period; we cannot adjust for temporal shifts in labeling.
- Related codes’ direction over time cannot be assessed; in this window, C2 is present in 241/1,018 and C6 in 207/1,018, but directionality is unknown [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]].

Counter-evidence
- Rival barriers are also prominent in the same stage: material & digital-physical gap (C2) at 241/1,018, price (C6) at 207/1,018, and fulfilment (C7) at 140/1,018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]]. Interpretation: If absolute counts for C1 were stable while other topics fell, C1’s share could rise without a true increase in underlying concern; this corpus cannot distinguish such patterns over time.

Confidence
- Medium. C1 has sufficient volume in this window (189/1,018 across 4 sources) and is labeled reliably (kappa 0.657) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]]. However, overall validation thresholds fail and the corpus spans roughly three independent source types, limiting robustness [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]], [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].

Limitations
- This is discussion share, not behavior; no funnel or conversion data exists here [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- The corpus was collected in a single window; it cannot show trends or year‑over‑year change. Interpretation: No date distribution is available to test whether C1 is worse now than two years ago.
- Relevance is narrowly defined, with hand‑read implied recall near 45%, and exclusions skew toward price/value and delivery/trust; barrier shares are conditional on this rubric [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Two validation thresholds fail; only 2 of 5 measurable codes clear the 0.60 kappa threshold; relevance recall is an estimate below target [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].
- Source independence is limited to roughly three types; app‑store reviews are skewed, and store scraping contributes volume disproportionate to signal [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]], [[analysis_method_flags|store_scrape_low_yield]].
- Only about 36% of relevant records are Myntra‑specific; most evidence reflects Indian online fashion generally [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Low counts cannot be ranked confidently; Stage A is under‑detected by construction [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]], [[analysis_method_flags|stage_a_underdetection]].
- Interpretation: For C3 and C4, the brief is too thin to report fine‑grained “how often” by time or to test source‑stable trends; we mention their presence but do not rank them over time.

results.question: Which specific brands do people say run small?
results.restated: Which specific brands do people say 'run small' (i.e., which brands are mentioned as having sizing that runs small)?
results.answer:
Answer
Correction: This corpus does not support brand-level findings; barriers are not classified by brand, so no brand-level comparison exists. Interpretation: We can speak to the share of discussion about the gap called Fit & size uncertainty (C1), including how people phrase “runs small,” but not which specific brands are said to run small.

Evidence
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1) appears in 189 of 1018 coded records, raised by 185 distinct authors, from 4 sources, with mean confidence 0.816 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]].
- By source: YouTube 144 of 573; Reddit 40 of 309; Play 3 of 114; App Store 2 of 22 [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]], [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]].
- Coding reliability for C1 clears the reliability threshold (kappa 0.657; verdict “reliable”) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]].
- Evidence-strength composite for C1 is 0.69 with source_diversity reported as 1; counterfactual rate 0.026 and workaround rate 0.09 across n=189 [[analysis_evidence_strength|C1]].

In users' words
- “levi's jeans are labelled smaller than the actual size...and also..one jean that would have fit u properly at a particular size, at the same size another jeans may not fit u.” [[rec|dff1e8c42ec7425a8260683d42a33b842ef9265c]]
- “brand size small 36,medium=38,large=40” [[rec|b951e8a49b705356628dd51c12fa274f58375393]]
- “but I am not sure about what size I should pick.” [[rec|7eb687e99df800b84c2f83bf2400411e30f30ee1]]
- “people my size” [[rec|a7494a411fbdbf6f9aa9b85f374ad9addc08d8af]]

Variation
- By source type, mentions of Fit & size uncertainty (C1) are most often from YouTube (144 of 573) and next from Reddit (40 of 309), with very small counts from Play (3 of 114) and App Store (2 of 22) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]], [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]].
- Interpretation: The corpus does not include brand- or product-level structured fields, so no brand-level comparison or per-brand author/source split is available.

Counter-evidence
- Other confidence-phase barriers are raised more often or similarly often in the same discussions: Material & digital-physical gap (C2) 241 of 1018; Price (C6) 207 of 1018; Styling & self-image (C3) 154 of 1018; Fulfilment (C7) 140 of 1018; External validation & social proof (C4) 82 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]].
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1) co-occurs above chance with Styling & self-image (C3) at 40 joint records and with External validation & social proof (C4) at 17 joint records, indicating sizing is often discussed alongside other concerns rather than alone [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C3]], [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C4]].
- C1 also co-occurs with C10 at 37 joint records, but C10 is marked unreliable; any inference involving that pairing must carry this caveat [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]], [[analysis_method_flags|c10_unreliable]].
- Interpretation: The corpus does not show brand-level contradictions (e.g., the same brand “runs small” vs “true/large”) because brands are not systematically captured.

Confidence
- Medium. C1 coding is reliable (kappa 0.657) and supported by 189 records across multiple sources [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]]. However, the evidence-strength composite is 0.69 and overall metric thresholds include reported failures, which tempers confidence [[analysis_evidence_strength|C1]], [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].

Limitations
- Interpretation: No brand-level structured fields exist; the dataset cannot attribute “runs small” to specific brands.
- Every share reported is a share of discussion, not shopper behavior; no funnel or conversion data exists here [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow, with excluded material skewing toward price/value and delivery/trust; rankings reflect a constrained view of what people discuss [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Only about 36% of relevant records are Myntra-specific; most discussion is about Indian online fashion generally [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- App-store sources are not independent from each other, so triangulation relies on roughly three independent source types, not four [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Validation thresholds: two fail; relevance recall is estimated at about 79% against an 85% threshold [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].
- Counts below 30 are reportable but never rankable; below 15 are not shown as findings. Interpretation: Any per-brand claim would need at least this volume before ranking confidence, which the corpus cannot currently provide [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].

What counts as “runs small” here, and coding consistency
- Interpretation: Phrases that indicate “runs small” appear in user text and are captured under Fit & size uncertainty (C1), for example “labelled smaller than the actual size” and “brand size small 36,medium=38,large=40” [[rec|dff1e8c42ec7425a8260683d42a33b842ef9265c]], [[rec|b951e8a49b705356628dd51c12fa274f58375393]].
- Coding for C1 is reliable (kappa 0.657), indicating consistent capture of sizing-uncertainty language across a gold-labeled subset [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]].

What would overturn a brand-level “runs small” claim, and sample size needs
- Interpretation: Given the absence of brand fields, a credible brand-level claim would require structured brand attribution plus enough brand-linked records to surpass reporting floors.
- The method floor states that a count below 30 is reportable but never rankable, and below 15 is not shown as a finding at all; applying this standard would be a prerequisite for treating a per-brand statement as more than anecdotal [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].

premise.correction: This corpus does not contain brand or product-level structured fields; it only holds discussion coded to barriers like C1 (fit & size uncertainty). Therefore it cannot reliably report which specific brands are said to run small.

gate_reasons: barriers are not classified by brand, so no brand-level comparison exists

results.question: Do people who abandon at checkout come back later?
results.restated: Do people who abandon at checkout (the stage-D 'checkout' exits) come back later to complete the purchase?
results.answer:
Answer
Correction: The corpus cannot trace whether the same person who left checkout later returned to complete the purchase; it only captures discussion-level signals (Exit vs Defer and occasional explicit statements). Interpretation: We can partially answer with how often checkout-stage barriers are raised in discussion and what people say about exits vs deferrals, but the evidence is thin for D4 and not longitudinal, so we cannot say who actually came back to buy.

Evidence
- How much discussion is about checkout-stage problems (D1–D4) and specifically Final reconsideration (D4)
  - Across checkout stage (stage D), exits are raised in 50 of 1,018 records [[analysis_stage_outcome|D|exit]].
  - Cost surprise (D1): 14 records, 14 distinct authors, across 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|D1]].
  - Mechanical friction (D2): 22 records, 22 distinct authors, across 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|D2]].
  - Late-revealed terms (D3): 26 records, 26 distinct authors, across 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|D3]].
  - Final reconsideration (D4): 9 records, 9 distinct authors, across 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|D4]].
- Exit vs Defer for checkout problems
  - Interpretation: At stage D, the table shows exits but does not report defers; only exit counts are available for D in this run [[analysis_stage_outcome|D|exit]].
- Distinct authors and source mix
  - Distinct authors by code at checkout: D1 (14), D2 (22), D3 (26), D4 (9) [[analysis_code_prevalence|D1]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|D2]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|D3]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|D4]].
  - By source for D4: Google Play 4, YouTube 3, Reddit 1, App Store 1 [[analysis_source_code|play|D4]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|D4]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|D4]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|D4]].
  - By source for other checkout codes (for context):
    - D1: Play 8, YouTube 5, Reddit 1 [[analysis_source_code|play|D1]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|D1]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|D1]]
    - D2: YouTube 12, Play 8, Reddit 1, App Store 1 [[analysis_source_code|youtube|D2]], [[analysis_source_code|play|D2]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|D2]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|D2]]
    - D3: Play 13, YouTube 6, Reddit 6, App Store 1 [[analysis_source_code|play|D3]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|D3]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|D3]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|D3]]
- Explicit statements about returning later to complete purchase vs never returning
  - Interpretation: Among the provided records, none explicitly state that a buyer abandoned at checkout and later completed the purchase; some do express permanent exit sentiments (see “In users’ words” and Counter-evidence).

In users' words
- Cost surprise at checkout: “I paid ₹700+ more than the MRP” [[rec|893ede648353cc8d160309de57577ec7530ce63a]].
- Late-revealed terms affecting the decision: “there is no return or exchange option available for this product” [[rec|893ede648353cc8d160309de57577ec7530ce63a]].
- Final reconsideration pressure from policy changes: “add more amount of product to use your mycash.. it is completely unfair” [[rec|9d842ea675d0be8077b6ce7f6563490b53d5fb04]].
- Payment preference at checkout: “pay later option best hai” [[rec|fcaca1d738b9ea244b2a55d43236fef01275e782]].

Variation
- Source mix for Final reconsideration (D4) spans Google Play, YouTube, Reddit, and the App Store with small counts in each: 4, 3, 1, and 1 respectively [[analysis_source_code|play|D4]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|D4]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|D4]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|D4]].
- Interpretation: Counts for D4 are below the reportability floor, so we cannot say whether any source is over-represented; the largest single-source count is 4, which is under the threshold to generalize [[analysis_code_prevalence|D4]], [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].

Counter-evidence
- Records include firm “never return” sentiments after bad experiences, which cut against the idea that most checkout exits are temporary: “never ordering from this app again” [[rec|b28005c42d6d764f5fa6f3e6fdf38a47d8c59606]].
- At the same time, discussion includes counterfactuals that imagine conditions under which the purchase might proceed, especially for Final reconsideration: 5 counterfactuals out of 9 D4-coded records [[analysis_counterfactuals|D4]]. Interpretation: Counterfactuals show people describing what would have changed their decision, but they do not demonstrate that they actually returned and completed checkout.

Confidence
Low. The key checkout reconsideration signal (Final reconsideration, D4) has 9 records and 9 authors [[analysis_code_prevalence|D4]], below the minimum count to support strong claims [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]]. Reliability for D1–D3 is “not measurable” due to too few gold labels, so code-level agreement cannot be verified [[analysis_gold_agreement|D1]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|D2]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|D3]]. Shares are discussion shares, not behavioral rates [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].

Limitations
- No longitudinal or funnel data: discussion shares cannot show whether individuals who exited later returned to complete checkout [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- Thin evidence for D4: counts are below the floor needed for stable inference [[analysis_code_prevalence|D4]], [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].
- Classifier validation thresholds fail on key metrics; code reliability for these checkout codes is not measurable on gold labels [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|D1]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|D2]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|D3]].
- Source independence is limited (app stores share the same skew; Reddit via a third party), so cross-source triangulation is weaker than four fully independent sources [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow and likely under-represents price/value and delivery/trust topics, so rankings and shares are conditional on that rubric [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Only about 36% of the relevant corpus is Myntra-specific; platform-mechanical checkout codes rely on a smaller Myntra pool [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Segments are derived, not observed; any lift of confidence-phase signals into undecided groups is partly circular [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].

premise.asserts: That checkout abandonments are traceable as 'returns later' in the corpus
premise.correction: The corpus contains only discussion-level signals (Exit vs Defer and occasional explicit statements); it does not contain user-level longitudinal purchase records, so it cannot directly measure whether the same people returned later to complete checkout.

gate_reasons: too few records for how often this is raised — D4 is under the 15 needed
too few records for whether this holds up across sources — the largest count is 13, under the 15 needed to report it
too few records for how well-supported this is — the largest count is 14, under the 15 needed to report it
records are not linked to individuals over time, so no one can be followed

results.question: What share of wishlist saves are gifts for other people?
results.restated: What share of wishlist saves are intended as gifts for other people?
results.answer:
Answer
Correction: The corpus records what people say about why they didn’t buy after saving; it does not measure what share of all wishlist saves are gifts. Interpretation: Whether a save was intended as a gift is not a coded dimension here, so we can only point to adjacent signals and a single explicit anecdote, not a share.

Evidence
- External validation & social proof (C10) is discussed in 68 of 1018 posts, by 67 distinct authors, across 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]].
- Intent extinguished after saving (C11) appears in 24 of 1018 posts, by 24 authors, across 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C11]].
- Intent never existed (C9) appears in 21 of 1018 posts, by 21 authors, across 2 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C9]].
- Action trigger (journey stage) (C13) appears in 51 of 1018 posts, by 50 authors, across 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]].
- External validation & social proof — reviews/word of mouth (C4) appears in 82 of 1018 posts, by 80 authors, across 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]].
- The single explicit gifting anecdote we have is coded as C11; C11 co-occurs with Price (C6) 15 times out of 24 C11 posts [[analysis_cooccurrence|C11|C6]].
- By source, C10 is discussed more on YouTube (54 of 573) than on Reddit (13 of 309) or the App Store (1 of 22) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C10]][[analysis_source_code|reddit|C10]][[analysis_source_code|appstore|C10]].
- Interpretation: Mentions of gift-intent are not coded, so we cannot count how many distinct authors discussed gifting as the reason for saving, nor test co-occurrence of a “gift” dimension with other codes.

In users' words
- “I kept that purse in wishlist so we could buy that purse on a sale or something.” [[rec|9b26643264276659111220430e855970f5f9169a]]
- “A few days back, I saw there was a mother's day sale and bought it to surprise her on mother's day.” [[rec|9b26643264276659111220430e855970f5f9169a]]
- “Bro pls share shirt site i want this shirt” [[rec|f6ab45e5f6a02d9184c2f15df202bf42570ad602]]
- “see how many posts, comments and reviews did it get and then go ahead.” [[rec|0afe1663f365d89029adf08a61c57bd3b6f623c7]]

Variation
- Interpretation: Because gift-intent is not a coded dimension, the corpus cannot show variation by source for “saves intended as gifts.”
- For adjacent signals, C10 is discussed across sources, with counts highest on YouTube and lower on Reddit and the App Store [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C10]][[analysis_source_code|reddit|C10]][[analysis_source_code|appstore|C10]].
- Interpretation: The one explicit gifting anecdote we have is on Reddit, but a single anecdote is too thin to generalize across sources; this aligns with the minimum-n guidance on small cells [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].

Counter-evidence
- Rival barriers dominate the discussion: the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) appears in 241 of 1018 posts, Price (C6) in 207 of 1018, Fit & size uncertainty (C1) in 189 of 1018, Styling & self-image (C3) in 154 of 1018, and Fulfilment (C7) in 140 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]].
- Interpretation: If a large share of saves were gifts, we would expect frequent, multi-source mentions of gifting as the reason for saving; instead, we only see one explicit anecdote and no code dedicated to gifts, which weighs against that claim.

Confidence
- Low. The key adjacent code (C10) is marked unreliable (kappa 0.10) and any claim resting on it must carry that caveat [[analysis_method_flags|c10_unreliable]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C10]]. Other relevant codes (C11, C13, C4) lack measurable reliability statistics [[analysis_gold_agreement|C11]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C13]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]]. Overall evaluation thresholds also failed on some metrics [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].

Limitations
- The corpus measures discussion, not behavior; no funnel or conversion data exists, so no share of saves (or gifts) can be estimated from this instrument [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- Interpretation: Whether a save was intended as a gift is not a coded dimension; any “gift” reading relies on manual interpretation of individual records rather than a tagged variable.
- Small-cell caution applies to thin signals and to any attempt to segment them by source [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow, with estimated recall below ideal and potential skew against price/value and delivery/trust topics; rankings reflect that scope, not the whole decision space [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Only about 36% of the relevant material is Myntra-specific; most discussion is about Indian fashion e-commerce generally [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Source triangulation spans roughly three independent source types, not four [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Segments are derived from classifications; any segment lift for confidence-stage codes is partly circular [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].

premise.asserts: that a measurable share of wishlist saves are gifts
premise.correction: The corpus records discussion about reasons items were not bought; it cannot estimate the share of all wishlist saves that are gifts because it contains no data on total saves or on representative user behavior.

gate_reasons: whether a save was intended as a gift is not a coded dimension
gate_caveats: whether this holds up across sources: too thin to report for C9, C11, C13, C4

results.question: Why is price the single biggest barrier to buying wishlisted items?

Answer
False premise: value & price uncertainty (Price [C6]) is not the single biggest barrier by share of discussion; the gap between how an item looks online and in person (Material & digital-physical gap [C2]) appears more often.
